instruction.name: xvld
instruction.description: Read whole vector from memory address `addr + offset`, save the data into `dst`. Address misalignment does not raise an exception. Note that you can use this intrinsic to load floating point vectors, even though the return type represents integer vectors.

experiments.name: operand dependency chain
experiments.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 250 --unroll2 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 20 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -2048; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; addi.d $r23, $r20, 128; li.d $r4, 8; st.d $r4, $r20, 0; li.d $r4, 0; st.d $r4, $r20, 8' --asm 'xvld $xr0, $r20, 0; xvst $xr0, $r23, 0; ld.d $r4, $r23, 0; add.d $r20, $r20, $r4'
experiments.notes: rj -> result chain through a vector store and a GPR load: the store-to-load forwarding (10.04 cycles) and the add.d (1 cycle) are subtracted, leaving the 4-cycle vector load.

latencies.notes: rj -> result chain through a vector store and a GPR load: the store-to-load forwarding (10.04 cycles) and the add.d (1 cycle) are subtracted, leaving the 4-cycle vector load.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: xvld $xr0, $r20, 0; xvld $xr1, $r20, 32; xvld $xr2, $r20, 64; xvld $xr3, $r20, 96; xvld $xr4, $r20, 128; xvld $xr5, $r20, 160; xvld $xr6, $r20, 192; xvld $xr7, $r20, 224
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r4, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r4' --asm 'xvld $xr0, $r20, 0; xvld $xr1, $r20, 32; xvld $xr2, $r20, 64; xvld $xr3, $r20, 96; xvld $xr4, $r20, 128; xvld $xr5, $r20, 160; xvld $xr6, $r20, 192; xvld $xr7, $r20, 224'
throughput.notes: 8 independent memory operations take 4.01 cycles. Buffer is 64-byte aligned; unaligned LASX loads/stores are substantially slower. The measured CPI 0.5012 is the nominal 0.5 within measurement noise; the value is reported as the nominal figure.

notes: L1D-hit vector load latency is 4 cycles, the same as the scalar floating-point loads.
